title: Processes vs Threads & Process Memory Layout
scope: What a process and a thread each own (address space, file descriptors, signal handlers are process-wide; stack, registers, thread-local storage are per-thread), the address-space layout (text, initialized/uninitialized data, heap, stack, and where thread stacks live relative to the main stack), and why threads make some bugs process-invisible.
figs: procmem: one process's address space with a shared heap/data segment and multiple thread stacks

title: Process Control: fork, exec, wait, signals
scope: fork()'s copy-on-write duplication and what is and is not inherited, the exec family replacing the image, wait/waitpid and orphan/zombie processes, signal delivery and default dispositions, signal handlers and async-signal-safe functions (POSIX's actual list), and why fork() in a multithreaded process is dangerous.
figs: forkmodel: parent/child address spaces after fork with copy-on-write pages, and a process tree waiting on a child

title: POSIX Threads: Creation, Joining & Attributes
scope: pthread_create's signature and start routine contract, pthread_join vs pthread_detach and the resource-leak risk of neither, pthread_attr_t (stack size, guard size, detach state, scheduling policy), passing and returning data safely through the void* argument, and thread-local storage with __thread / _Thread_local.

title: Mutexes & Critical Sections
scope: pthread_mutex_init/lock/unlock/destroy semantics, mutex types (PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL/RECURSIVE/ERRORCHECK) and when each matters, spinlocks vs mutexes and when spinning is actually faster, critical section sizing, and a real compiled example that reproduces a race with the lock removed and fixes it with the lock added.
figs: mutexstate: two threads contending for one mutex, with the blocked thread's wait and wake shown on a timeline

title: Condition Variables & Signaling
scope: pthread_cond_wait/signal/broadcast and why a condition variable is always used with a mutex and a predicate loop (never a bare wait), lost wakeups and spurious wakeups and how the predicate loop prevents both, signal vs broadcast, and building a bounded blocking queue from a mutex plus two condition variables (not-empty, not-full).
figs: condvarflow: producer signaling a waiting consumer through a mutex-protected condition variable, with the predicate check on wake

title: Semaphores, Read-Write Locks & Barriers
scope: POSIX unnamed and named semaphores (sem_init/sem_post/sem_wait) as counting resource guards versus a mutex's binary ownership, pthread_rwlock for read-heavy workloads and the writer-starvation risk, and pthread_barrier_wait for phased parallel work, each with a compiled example.
figs: rwlock: multiple concurrent readers versus one exclusive writer on the same rwlock, and a writer waiting for readers to drain

title: Memory Model, Atomics & Ordering
scope: The C11 abstract memory model, stdatomic.h types and operations, the memory_order variants (relaxed, acquire, release, acq_rel, seq_cst) and what each actually orders, compiler reordering versus CPU reordering versus cache-coherence effects, false sharing across cache lines, and why volatile is neither atomic nor a memory barrier (ties back to the C page's qualifier module).
figs: memorder: a store-then-flag-set on one thread and a flag-check-then-load on another, showing what an acquire/release pair actually prevents

title: Deadlock, Livelock, Starvation & Priority Inversion
scope: The four necessary deadlock conditions and which one lock ordering breaks, try-lock and timeout-based avoidance, livelock (two threads politely deadlocking by both backing off in lockstep), starvation under an unfair scheduler or lock, and priority inversion with the priority-inheritance-mutex fix (the Mars Pathfinder story is fair game to mention, briefly).
figs: deadlock: two threads each holding one lock and waiting on the other's, as a wait-for cycle

title: Classic Concurrency Problems
scope: Producer-consumer with a bounded buffer, the readers-writers problem with both the naive and starvation-avoiding solutions, and dining philosophers with the resource-ordering fix that avoids the deadlock, each as real compiled pthreads code with the bug reproduced before the fix.
figs: diningphil: five philosophers and five forks as a circular resource graph, with the asymmetric fix that breaks the cycle

title: Thread-Safety Patterns & Lock-Free Basics
scope: Reentrant vs thread-safe (a function can be one without the other), thread-local storage as a lock-free technique, double-checked locking done correctly with C11 atomics (and why the naive version is broken), compare-and-swap and a simple lock-free counter, and where an application engineer should stop and reach for a library instead of hand-rolling lock-free structures.

title: OS Scheduling & Real-Time Concurrency
scope: Preemptive multitasking basics, Linux scheduling policies (SCHED_OTHER, SCHED_FIFO, SCHED_RR) and nice/priority, context-switch cost and why it matters for high-IOPS validation code, and what changes when a task has a real deadline (priority assignment, avoiding page faults and unbounded locks in the hot path).
figs: scheduling: several threads' run/ready/blocked states over time under a preemptive scheduler

title: Inter-Process Communication
scope: Anonymous and named pipes, POSIX message queues (mq_open/mq_send/mq_receive), shared memory (shm_open/mmap) with an explicit synchronization primitive since shared memory itself provides none, and signals as a lightweight control-plane mechanism, contrasted with the in-process primitives from modules 4 to 6.
figs: ipcmodel: two processes exchanging data via a pipe, a message queue, and shared memory, with what synchronization each needs

title: Virtual Memory & mmap
scope: Paging, the page table's role, and what a page fault actually does; mmap for file-backed and anonymous memory, MAP_SHARED vs MAP_PRIVATE, msync, and memory-mapped I/O in firmware/embedded validation code (mapping a register file via /dev/mem-style access) as the concrete tie to module 1's address-space picture.
figs: vmpaging: a virtual address translating through a page table to a physical frame, with a fault on an unmapped page

title: Interrupts, ISRs & Embedded Concurrency
scope: Interrupt context versus normal thread/task context, why an ISR must never block (no mutex, no malloc, no blocking syscall), disabling interrupts versus taking a lock as two different concurrency tools, top-half/bottom-half (or hardirq/softirq, tasklet) style splits for deferring work, and reentrancy when the same ISR can interrupt itself or another ISR.
figs: isrflow: normal task execution interrupted by an ISR, with the top half doing minimal work and handing off to a deferred bottom half

title: Debugging Concurrency & Principal-Level Design
scope: Finding real races with ThreadSanitizer and helgrind, the difference between a Heisenbug that vanishes under a debugger and one that needs stress plus sanitizers, and Principal-level design-and-code questions: a fixed-size thread pool with a work queue, a strategy for a system with many locks that provably avoids deadlock, and a bounded blocking queue built and reasoned about from first principles (ties back to module 5).
figs: threadpool: a shared work queue with several worker threads pulling tasks under one mutex and one condition variable
